correctness.rationale: The Hilbert-space Green formula exactly gives norm squared F(x)/L-J/(2L^2). A valid resistance interpolation identity on each metric edge makes F quadratic with positive strict concavity coefficients. Rank-one inversion of the K_n Laplacian gives all three vertex resistance orbits; symbolic cancellation checks the three globally compared maxima. For n>=5 the convex Q_n has negative endpoints on [0,1], while n=4 has exactly one interior root sqrt(5)-2; the h>1 and h=1 regimes follow from strict pairwise differences and symmetry. Equality cases follow from Riesz/Cauchy–Schwarz. Standalone SymPy and six exact subdivided-network tests executed. No finite sampling is used as proof of a universal quantifier.
